title: Best Whole House Dehumidifier (2026): Ducted & Central Picks
dek: When every room feels clammy, one central machine beats three portables. These are the ducted and basement units worth plumbing in.
description: The best whole house dehumidifiers of 2026 from Aprilaire, AlorAir and Santa Fe, compared on AHAM capacity, coverage, cost, drainage and install type.
intro: Some humidity problems refuse to stay in one room. The upstairs bedrooms feel sticky, the basement smells musty, and the windows sweat on cool mornings all over the house. You can chase that with a portable in every damp corner, emptying buckets as you go, or you can install one **whole house dehumidifier** (also sold as a whole-home dehumidifier) that dries the entire home to a single setpoint and drains itself for good.

Whole-house units either tie into your HVAC system's return duct or sit centrally in a basement or crawl space and push dry air outward. They're rated in professional AHAM pints, carry five- to six-year warranties, and cost far more up front than any portable. It's also the one category where spending more reliably buys you drier air, so it pays to choose carefully.

We compared the current ducted and central models on rated capacity, coverage, efficiency recognition, drainage, low-temperature operation and warranty, then read installer notes and owner reports for long-term reliability. Here's how the field shakes out.
topPicksLead: The **Aprilaire E100** is our top pick for most homes: it has the capacity to dry a large house from one spot, top-tier efficiency, and the flexibility to run ducted or freestanding.

products.name: Aprilaire E100 Whole-House Dehumidifier
pros: Up to 100 pints a day for homes to roughly 5,500 sq ft
Washable filter and no tank to empty
cons: Professional installation recommended for ducted setups
Premium cost compared with value brands
products.whyWeLoveIt: The E100 is the benchmark every other whole-house unit gets measured against. It has enough extraction to handle a large home from one central location, and its efficiency recognition means season-long running doesn't punish your power bill the way a row of portables would.
products.performance: Aprilaire rates it at up to 100 pints a day with coverage up to about 5,500 square feet, and you can either connect it to the HVAC return or let it stand alone in a basement or crawl space. It's assembled in the USA around a corrosion-resistant coil, and once the condensate line is plumbed, owners describe it as close to maintenance-free beyond rinsing the filter. The full E-Series ladder is broken down in our [best Aprilaire dehumidifier](/best/best-aprilaire-dehumidifier/) guide.
products.notes: Plan a gravity drain path before installation day. Without a floor drain or sump nearby, you'll need a separate condensate pump.

products.name: AlorAir Sentinel HDi90 Dehumidifier
pros: 90 pints a day at AHAM conditions
cons: The 198-pint saturation figure in listings can mislead shoppers
Rated coverage is smaller than the Aprilaire E100's
products.whyWeLoveIt: AlorAir delivers commercial-style extraction without premium-brand pricing. The HDi90 adds something the E100 lacks, a built-in pump, so you can install it far from a drain and still run it unattended.
products.performance: AlorAir lists 90 pints a day at AHAM conditions (80°F, 60% RH) and 198 pints at saturation, with coverage up to roughly 2,600 square feet. Epoxy-coated coils and a defrost cycle that works down to about 33.8°F make it just as comfortable in a chilly basement as tied into ductwork upstairs. For how the two brands differ on price, pumps and warranty terms, see our [AlorAir vs. Aprilaire comparison](/compare/alorair-vs-aprilaire-dehumidifier/).

products.name: Santa Fe Ultra V100 Ventilating Dehumidifier
pros: 100 pints a day for fully ducted installs
cons: Rated for about 2,300 sq ft, less than the E100
products.whyWeLoveIt: Santa Fe is the name HVAC contractors tend to bring up first, and the Ultra V100 behaves more like an air-quality system than an appliance. It dries, filters through MERV-13 media and brings in measured outdoor air, all from one cabinet.
products.performance: Santa Fe rates it at 100 pints a day for spaces up to roughly 2,300 square feet. It replaced the Ultra98, which Santa Fe discontinued on February 17, 2026, and it runs on the newer R454B refrigerant. For allergy-prone households or humid-climate homes where the unit runs most of the year, the filtration and ventilation earn their keep. See the rest of the lineup in our [best Santa Fe dehumidifier](/best/best-santa-fe-dehumidifier/) guide.

products.name: Aprilaire E080 Pro Dehumidifier

Same ENERGY STAR Most Efficient recognition as the E100

products.whyWeLoveIt: If the E100 is more machine than your house needs, the E080 is the same design one step down. You keep the efficiency recognition, the warranty and the ducted-or-freestanding flexibility for meaningfully less money.
products.performance: Aprilaire rates it at 80 pints a day with coverage up to about 4,400 square feet, which suits a typical 2,000 to 3,000 square foot home outside the most humid regions. The slightly smaller cabinet slides into crawl spaces and closets where the E100 gets tight. For many households it's a better fit than stretching a big portable past its limits.

products.name: AlorAir Sentinel HDi65S Dehumidifier
pros: Built-in pump lifts water up to about 19.6 ft
cons: 55 pints AHAM is basement-scale, not whole-home ducted scale
Won't fully dry upper floors in a very humid climate
products.whyWeLoveIt: A lot of whole-house dampness starts below grade and gets pulled upward by the stack effect. Drying the basement or crawl space at the source often fixes the floors above, and the HDi65S is the most affordable way here to do that with a real pump and crawl-space-grade build.
products.performance: AlorAir lists 55 pints a day at AHAM conditions and 120 at saturation, which is right-sized for a whole basement or encapsulated crawl space. The pump and low-temperature defrost let it run unattended in cold, drain-less spaces. It's also a favorite in our [best crawl space dehumidifier](/best/best-crawl-space-dehumidifier/) roundup.

products.name: hOmeLabs 50-Pint Wi-Fi Dehumidifier with Pump (HME1003)
pros: Built-in pump drains up to about 16 ft
Rated for about 4,500 sq ft of open space
cons: Closed doors and hallways limit its reach
products.whyWeLoveIt: No portable is truly a whole-house dehumidifier, and we won't pretend otherwise. But if your problem is really one damp floor, or you rent and can't touch the ductwork, a high-capacity pump portable placed centrally captures much of the benefit at a fraction of the installed cost.
products.performance: It's a 50-pint-class unit under the DOE test, with roughly 218 CFM of airflow and a pump that pushes water up to about 16 feet, so it can run for days without attention. It makes a sensible stepping stone: if it can't keep a floor below 50%, you've learned that a ducted unit is worth the investment. More self-draining options are in our [best dehumidifier with pump](/best/best-dehumidifier-with-pump/) guide.

blocks.text: The mold window is the strongest argument for a permanently drained central unit. A portable's bucket can fill at 10 a.m. and sit there until you get home; a plumbed whole-house machine just keeps going. And because whole-house units remove more water per kilowatt-hour, the best of them can cost less to run than the two or three portables they replace. Our [energy-efficient dehumidifier](/best/best-energy-efficient-dehumidifier/) guide explains what the Most Efficient badge means.

We don't install units in a test house and log readings, and we won't pretend to. Instead, we start from published, comparable data: AHAM-condition capacity ratings, ENERGY STAR listings, manufacturer coverage claims and installation manuals for drainage, ducting and minimum operating temperature.

From there, we weighted real-world capacity highest, followed by efficiency (these machines run for months), drainage options, low-temperature behavior for basements and crawl spaces, and warranty length. We read installer commentary and owner reviews for patterns like failed pumps, frozen coils and condensate leaks, and we checked CPSC records for recalls. Lifespan data came from the same sources summarized in our [how long do dehumidifiers last](/guides/how-long-do-dehumidifiers-last/) guide.

sections.heading: What to look for in a whole-house dehumidifier

items.label: AHAM pints, not saturation pints
items.text: Many listings show two numbers. The saturation figure (90°F, 90% RH) flatters every machine; the AHAM figure (80°F, 60% RH) predicts how it behaves in a lived-in house. A "198-pint" unit and a "90-pint" unit can be the same box.

items.label: Capacity matched to your home
items.text: Use the sizing ladder below and round up rather than down. A slightly larger unit cycles less and holds the setpoint more easily.

items.label: Ducted or freestanding
items.text: Ducted installs dry every room evenly through your HVAC. Freestanding units in a basement or crawl space cost less to install and still fix a lot of whole-home dampness. Our [whole-house dehumidifier installation guide](/guides/whole-house-dehumidifier-installation/) walks through both.
sub: Ducted: best for multi-story homes with sticky upper floors
Freestanding: best when the problem starts below grade

items.label: A drain plan
items.text: These run continuously, so there's no tank. You need a gravity line to a floor drain or sump, or a model with a built-in pump.

items.label: Warranty length
items.text: Five to six years is standard here. The compressor is the part that fails, so coverage length is a large share of what you're paying for.

sections.heading: Whole house dehumidifier cost: is it worth it?

head: Whole-house unit

blocks.text: If more than one room regularly sits above 50 to 60% humidity, a whole-house unit usually justifies its cost through even drying, zero bucket duty and longer life. If only one room is damp, a good portable is still the smarter buy.

blocks.title: Running cost, roughly
blocks.text: A 500-watt-class unit running about half the day costs around $30 a month at the EIA's US average residential rate of roughly 16.5 cents per kWh. Your climate and setpoint move that number far more than the brand does.

For most homes, the **Aprilaire E100** is the whole-house dehumidifier to buy: big capacity, top efficiency and a choice of ducted or freestanding installation. The **AlorAir Sentinel HDi90** brings ducted drying and a built-in pump for less, the **Santa Fe Ultra V100** adds MERV-13 filtration and fresh-air ventilation, and the **Aprilaire E080** right-sizes the formula for mid-size homes. If your dampness starts in the basement, the **AlorAir HDi65S** fixes it at the source, and if you can't install anything, the **hOmeLabs HME1003** is an honest stopgap for one floor.

faqs.q: What is the best whole-house dehumidifier?
faqs.a: The Aprilaire E100 suits most homes. It's rated at up to 100 pints a day for homes up to about 5,500 sq ft, carries ENERGY STAR Most Efficient recognition, and installs ducted or freestanding. The AlorAir Sentinel HDi90 is the value pick, with 90 AHAM pints and a built-in pump.

faqs.q: How is a whole-house dehumidifier different from a portable?
faqs.a: A whole-house unit connects to your ductwork or sits centrally in a basement or crawl space, dries the entire home to one setpoint and drains permanently. A portable covers one room or floor, usually needs its bucket emptied or a hose rigged, and typically tops out around 50 DOE pints.

faqs.q: How much does a whole house dehumidifier cost?
faqs.a: Expect to pay from the high hundreds for a value ducted or basement unit to well over $2,000 for premium models like the Santa Fe Ultra V100, plus installation if you hire an HVAC contractor. Running costs are typically around $30 a month for a 500-watt-class unit working half the day, depending on climate and setpoint.

faqs.q: Why do whole-house units list two capacity numbers?
faqs.a: One is the saturation rating, measured at 90°F and 90% humidity; the other is the AHAM rating at 80°F and 60%. The AlorAir HDi90, for example, is listed at 198 pints at saturation and 90 pints AHAM. Compare models on the AHAM figure, which reflects normal living conditions.

faqs.q: What size whole-house dehumidifier do I need?
faqs.a: As a rule of thumb, about 65–80 AHAM pints a day for homes under 1,500 sq ft in a moderate climate, 90–100 for 1,500–2,500 sq ft or humid regions, and 120–155 for larger homes or Gulf Coast climates. Round up if you're between sizes.

faqs.q: What humidity should a whole-house dehumidifier hold?
faqs.a: Between 30% and 50% relative humidity, the range the EPA recommends, and never above 60%. Most owners set 45–50% in summer. Below 30%, you start to see static, dry sinuses and shrinking wood trim.

faqs.q: Can a whole house dehumidifier connect to my HVAC system?
faqs.a: Yes. Ducted units like the Aprilaire E100 and AlorAir HDi90 tie into the return side of a forced-air system so dry air reaches every room. That job is usually best left to an HVAC contractor; freestanding basement or crawl-space installs are more DIY-friendly. See our [installation guide](/guides/whole-house-dehumidifier-installation/) for what's involved.
